title: History of the Kazi and the Trickster's Cushion
summary: In the city of Aleppo presided a Chief Kazi who was so conceited that he believed himself immune to human weakness. He levied severe fines upon citizens for the smallest errors,...
keywords: history of the kazi who bare a babe
full_text:
In the city of Aleppo presided a Chief Kazi who was so conceited that he believed himself immune to human weakness. He levied severe fines upon citizens for the smallest errors, lecturing them from his velvet bench with unbearable self-righteousness.

A witty young scholar named Dalil, who had been unfairly fined by the Kazi for singing a joyful song in his own garden, resolved to teach the pompous judge an unforgettable lesson in humility.

Knowing that the Kazi was excessively superstitious and obsessed with bodily health, Dalil disguised himself as a foreign physician from Bukhara. He visited the Kazi, examined his pulse with exaggerated solemnity, and gasped in horror:
'Alas, your Excellency! A monstrous malady has seized your abdomen! The humors have congested into an extraordinary internal growth!'

The Kazi, trembling with panic, cried: 'Is it fatal, O Hakim? What can be done?'
Dalil replied: 'I shall prepare a marvelous herbal poultice to be bound across your waist with a silk sash under your outer robes. But beware! You must breathe gently, walk softly, and speak no harsh words for seven days, or the growth will rupture!'

Dalil placed a cleverly stuffed leather air-bladder beneath the Kazi's silk robe. Every day, the disguised physician visited to adjust the sash, secretly inflating the bladder further with a small hand bellows!
Within three days, the Kazi appeared so round and protruding beneath his gown that he could barely waddle!

Convinced he had contracted a bizarre swelling, the Kazi called his fellow judges to his bedside, weeping: 'Brothers, pray for me! An unnatural affliction has transformed my body!'

At that moment, Dalil entered with the Governor of Aleppo and several respected scholars.
'Fear not, your Excellency!' said Dalil. 'Let us perform the grand extraction!'
With a swift stroke of a lancet, Dalil punctured the concealed leather bladder! A long, loud whistling hiss escaped from the cushion as it deflated, filling the room with the scent of rosewater!

The Kazi looked down to find his belly completely flat, and the deflated leather cushion falling onto the carpet!
The Governor and the assembly roared with uncontrollable laughter.
Dalil bowed: 'Your Excellency, you see how easily a man can imagine himself carrying an impossible affliction when vanity and gullibility blind his reason. Henceforth, be gentle in judging the simple follies of citizens, for even a Chief Kazi can be tricked by a cushion of air!'

Cured of his pomposity, the Kazi returned the unjust fines and governed his courtroom with newfound modesty and genuine fairness.
moral: Pompous hypocrisy is easily punctured by sharp satire; those who judge others without self-awareness become laughingstocks.
